issuer: Colorado Department of Revenue, Taxation Division
title: Colorado DOR Private Letter Ruling PLR-26-004: Sales Tax Exemptions for Purchases of Medical Materials by Hospitals
summary: Sales of medicated dressings, nonmedicated dressings, bandages, gauze, and skin closure products to Company are exempt from sales tax provided they are intended to be furnished by a practitioner as part of professional services to patients.

Re: Sales of Medical Items to Provider
Dear XXXXXXXXX:
You submitted a request for a private letter ruling on behalf of XXXXXXXXX (the “Company”) to the
Colorado Department of Revenue (“Department”) pursuant to 1 CCR 201-1, Rule 24-35-103.5. This letter
is the Department’s private letter ruling. This ruling is binding on the Department to the extent set forth in
1 CCR 201-1, Rule 24-35-103.5. It cannot be relied upon by any taxpayer other than the taxpayer to
whom the ruling is made.
Issues
1. Whether sales of medicated dressings (antimicrobial silver dressings and antimicrobial
honey dressings and paste) to Company are exempt from sales tax.
2. Whether sales of nonmedicated dressings, bandages, and gauze to Company are exempt
from sales tax.
3. Whether sales of skin closure products to Company are exempt from sales tax.
Conclusions
1. Sales of medicated dressings (antimicrobial silver dressings and antimicrobial honey
dressings and paste) to Company are exempt from sales tax provided they are intended to
be furnished by a practitioner as part of professional services to patients.
2. Sales of nonmedicated dressings, bandages, and gauze to Company are exempt from
sales tax provided they are intended to be furnished by a practitioner as part of professional
services to patients.
3. Sales of skin closure products to Company are exempt from sales tax provided they are
intended to be furnished by a practitioner as part of professional services to patients.

Background1
Company owns healthcare facilities that provide long-term acute care and other medical services to help
patients with complex conditions recover, heal, and regain independence. Company purchases
medicated dressings, non-medicated dressings, and skin closure products from their medical suppliers for
use in their facilities.
1. Medicated Dressings
As required by federal law, the medicated dressings at issue (antimicrobial silver and antimicrobial honey
dressings and paste) may only be purchased by healthcare facilities under the authority of a licensed
physician or surgeon with prescribing privileges. They may be dispensed to patients only pursuant to an
order by a licensed practitioner during the medical treatment of their patients. The FDA product labeling
on the medicated dressings includes the “R Only” statement, which is required prior to dispensing and
X
delivering the items to a licensed practitioner or patient.
Antimicrobial silver dressings contain the substances silver nitrate or silver sulfadiazine, each of which is
a human prescription drug. After being applied onto the patient, the dressings treat wounds by releasing
antimicrobial silver ions and providing a barrier against contaminants.
Antimicrobial honey dressings and paste contain medical-grade honey and are applied onto the patient to
promote healing and prevent infection. The honey they contain is absorbed into the patient’s body and
aids wound healing through antibacterial action, reducing edema, promoting blood flow, and decreasing
pain and swelling.
2. Nonmedicated Dressings, Bandages, and Gauze
Nonmedicated dressings, bandages, and gauze purchased by Company are applied to the patient during
the medical service or are dispensed under the advice of a licensed physician. Licensed physicians
evaluate the patient and prescribe a specific dressing, bandage, or gauze to meet their clinical needs.
The nonmedicated dressings, bandages, and gauzes at issue are permanently transferred to a patient.
Some are consumed during the patient's hospital visit. However, many patients leave the hospital with the
dressing, bandage, or gauze in place to maintain proper wound healing or other treatment.
Nonmedicated dressings are applied directly over or around a wound, protecting and structurally
supporting fragile skin and tissue. They prevent distortions of form and function, both systemically and
otherwise.
Bandages are applied over or around a wound to help protect it, support proper healing, and manage its
environment. Additionally, some bandages help reduce swelling and improve blood flow.
Gauze, like dressings and bandages, is applied over or around a wound to protect, promote proper
healing of, and manage the environment of the wound. Gauze also supports weak or deformed areas by
protecting them from pressure and friction and by securing orthopedic splints, braces, and limbs in place.
3. Skin Closure Products
Skin closure products, specifically surgical skin closure devices and skin closure strips, are medical

devices that are applied to a patient’s skin over a wound. They are used to close wounds, attaching tissue
together by pulling or drawing the skin together. Skin closure products are intended to prevent infection
and encourage proper natural healing. In doing so, they prevent scarring, contractures, or impaired
mobility.
The surgical skin closure device is a sterile, single-use device that is made of fabric or plastic material
and intended to be applied to a part of a patient's body. It is held in place by pressure-sensitive adhesive
to secure objects to the skin, cover and protect wounds, or approximate the skin edges of a wound; it may
or may not include an absorbent pad. It is not intended for compression bandaging and is not an adhesive
tape nor an adhesive strip.
Skin closure strips are single-use, flexible bands made of fabric, plastic, paper, or other material that are
attached to a patient’s skin using pressure-sensitive adhesive. They are designed to keep a superficial
wound closed.
Discussion
Colorado imposes a sales tax on retail sales of tangible personal property.2 The term “tangible personal
property” means “corporeal personal property,” and generally embraces all goods, wares, merchandise,
products and commodities, and all tangible or corporeal things and substances that are dealt in and
capable of being possessed and exchanged.3 Medicated dressings, non-medicated dressings, and skin
closure products are tangible personal property, and as such they are subject to state sales and use tax if
their purchase is a retail sale and no specific exemption applies. Colorado allows sales tax exemptions for
qualifying sales of drugs, medical equipment, and supplies.4
Sales of medicated dressings (antimicrobial silver dressings and antimicrobial honey dressings and
paste) to Company are exempt from sales tax provided they are intended to be furnished by a practitioner
as part of professional services to patients. Sales of prescription drugs that are furnished by a practitioner
as part of professional services provided to patients are exempt from tax.5 An item is “furnished to a
patient” when it is “provided to a patient to take with them when they leave the practitioner’s facility” or
“administered … topically” so that it “is absorbed into the patient’s body.”6 Company purchases medicated
dressings labeled “Rx only” and dispenses them in accordance with a prescription. Consequently, sales
of “Rx only” medicated dressings (antimicrobial silver dressings and antimicrobial honey dressings and
paste) to Company are exempt from sales tax.
Sales of nonmedicated dressings, bandages, gauze, and skin closure products to Company are exempt
from sales tax provided they are intended to be furnished by a practitioner as part of professional services
to patients. Sales of nonprescription materials that are furnished by a practitioner as part of professional
services are exempt from tax.7 “[B]andages, arm slings, packages of topical antiseptics and topical pain
relief balms that are provided by a practitioner to a patient for use outside the practitioner's facility are
furnished to a patient.”8 A practitioner is a person authorized by law to prescribe any drug or device,
acting within the scope of the authority.9 Nonmedicated dressings, bandages, and gauze purchased by
Company are applied to the patient during the medical service or are dispensed under the advice of a
licensed physician. Similarly, skin closure strips are attached to a patient’s skin using pressure-sensitive
adhesive. These items are either consumed during the patient's hospital visit or leave the hospital with the
patient to maintain proper wound healing or other treatment. Therefore, sales of these items are exempt

Miscellaneous
This ruling is premised on the assumption that Company has completely and accurately disclosed all
material facts, that all representations are true and complete, and that Company has otherwise complied
with the requirements of section 24-35-103.5, C.R.S., and the rules promulgated pursuant thereto. The
Department reserves the right, among others, to independently evaluate Company’s facts,
representations, and assumptions. The ruling is null and void if any such fact, representation, or
assumption is incorrect and has a material bearing on the conclusions reached in this ruling. This ruling is
binding on the Department, and is subject to modification or revocation, in accordance with 1 CCR 201-1,
Rule 24-35-103.5.
The Department administers state and state-administered local sales and use taxes. This letter does not
address sales and use taxes administered by self-collected home-rule cities. You may wish to consult
with those local governments that administer their own sales or use taxes about the applicability of those
taxes. Visit our website at Tax.Colorado.gov for more information about state and local sales taxes.
Thank you for your request.
